articles.title: Serendipitous Lunar Graze
articles.summary: Robert A. Garfinkle details his serendipitous observation of a lunar graze occultation on September 6, 2000, from his home in Union City, California. While studying lunar features, he noticed stars from the M21 cluster approaching the Moon's dark limb. He successfully timed the total occultation of one star and the flickering graze of a brighter subgiant, noting its color changes as it skimmed the lunar south polar region.

articles.title: Lunar Graze and Straight Fault
articles.summary: The article features an unexpected lunar graze observation by Jane Houston Jones, highlighting lunar features like the Aitkin Basin and the Straight Fault (Rupes Recta), drawing geological parallels to Earth's San Andreas Fault. Additionally, Akkana Peck encourages public outreach through "Ecliptic Trick-or-Treating," suggesting observers share telescopic views of planets like Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn with Halloween trick-or-treaters.

articles.title: From Earth To The Moon
articles.summary: This article explores the geological similarities between Earth and the Moon, focusing on the formation and significance of lava tubes. The author details a visit to Lava Beds National Park, explaining how these natural conduits for flowing lava form and can eventually collapse to create features like sinuous rilles on both celestial bodies. Additionally, a brief section announces the acquisition of new telescopes for an astronomy club's loaner program.

articles.title: Binary Tour of Lyra
articles.summary: This document features an astronomical observing report detailing a 'binary tour' of the constellation Lyra, highlighting various double stars like Vega and Epsilon Lyrae, and emphasizing the joy of visual observing with amateur telescopes. It also includes an announcement for a club's December holiday party, outlining planned activities such as a potluck, show-and-tell, and a white elephant gift exchange, alongside a classifieds section for used astronomical equipment.

articles.title: David Morrison to Talk at Foothill College
articles.summary: Dr. David Morrison of NASA's Ames Research Center will deliver the inaugural lecture of the 2000-2001 Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series at Foothill College on October 11th. His talk will focus on near-Earth asteroids and comets, discussing their potential impact risks and current efforts to catalog them, as well as international discussions on planetary defense strategies. This free public event is cosponsored by NASA Ames, the Astronomical Society of the Pacific, and the SETI Institute, and aims to educate the public on a critical astronomical topic.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar October 2000
articles.summary: This article presents the "Celestial Calendar" for October 2000, detailing key astronomical events and data for observers. It includes lunar phases, rise/transit/set times, magnitudes, and celestial coordinates for the Sun and five nearer planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) throughout the month. Additionally, it provides astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and highlights the darkest Saturday night for optimal sky viewing.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner scope program. It details which telescopes are currently available for immediate loan, which are out on loan with their respective due dates, and which have extended loan periods. SJAA members interested in borrowing a scope are instructed to contact Mike Koop, and information about a waiting list is also provided.
